title: Why is Applied Digital Stock Falling and is it a Buy?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions.
summary: Parkevtate explains why Applied Digital (APLD) has crashed about 80% from its near-$50 high earlier in 2026 to about $12, down about 50% year to date, and whether it is a buy. It is not a demand problem: the company signs 15-year contracts with investment-grade hyperscalers and its backlog is in the tens of billions, with demand exceeding supply. The problem is funding the build-out - all the money goes up front while cash comes in monthly or quarterly. Its cost of debt was cut to 7% in June (a $1.6bn offering of 7% notes due 2031, down from 9.25%), but he would not be surprised if it is back toward 10% now, citing SpaceX paying close to 10% and the fallout from Nvidia's leadership turmoil and circular-financing scrutiny. Free cash flow stays negative until about 2030. He flags one oddity: CoreWeave, with over $50bn of long-term debt, is a customer (first Polaris Forge lease signed May 2025), which sits awkwardly with the strategy of only contracting with sound balance sheets. Call: APLD BUY reiterated (prior BUY 28 Oct), fair value $14.82, about 20% undervalued - but a weak call: 'one of the riskiest stocks in the market', only for very high risk tolerance, and he thinks other neo-clouds are better buys right now.

calls.base_case: Long-term hyperscaler contracts keep lenders comfortable; FCF turns positive in 2030 with exceptional growth after.
calls.bull_case: Funding costs stabilise; backlog converts and the stock re-rates well above the $14.82 fair value.
calls.bear_case: Capital gets harder/more expensive to raise (CoreWeave as a customer adds counterparty worry); dilution or stalled build-out caps revenue.
